LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Compound and not judgeable by eye. It tests two facts: Oak is used only as hairlines, and Oak covers no more than 5% of the designed area. Nobody can estimate a 5% area share by looking at a PNG. The hairline-only rule is stricter than the 5% cap, so it already implies it.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Rewrite each check as one fact, for example studio-launch H038: "Oak #C7A97A on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) appears only as thin hairline rules or dividers, never as a ground, panel, button, text or fill." Use the same wording for class-feed H037 and booking-story H035 with their own names and files. In the why, say the hairline-only wording covers the 5% cap.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Two independent facts in one check: no exclamation mark, and no discount or urgency wording. An output can fail one and pass the other.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Modify each check to keep only the wording fact, for example: "The copy on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) has no discount or urgency wording, such as sale, % off, limited time or hurry." Add a new check on each output: "The copy on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) has no exclamation mark." Do the same for class-feed.png and booking-story.png. Both new checks are K2_Q3, citing brand_identity.voice and price_positioning.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Asks for things a viewer cannot see in a flattened PNG: "full opacity" and "blend effect" are layer settings. "Tint" is unclear to a designer. It also packs five effects into one check.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Rewrite as the visible result, for example: "All type, the wordmark, and every ground, panel and button on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) is one flat, solid colour: nothing shows through it, and it has no gradient or drop shadow." Do the same for class-feed H035 and booking-story H032. The brand's 92% wordmark trap is still caught, because a 92% wordmark shows the ground through it.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Unclear jargon and two facts. "One content element" is not a term a designer checks at a glance. The check also mixes "the offer is grouped in one block" with "nothing covers it".
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Modify H002: "No photo, button, panel or other element covers any part of the class list on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png)." Add a new K1_Q1 check (source: acceptance_requirements, "one unobscured content element"): "The six classes and their prices on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) sit together in one block, not split across separate parts of the page."

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Two independent cut-out defects in one check: the edge biting into the figure, and a halo or fringe. A cut-out can have either defect without the other.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Modify H013: "The cut-out edge around the instructor on “Class announcement” (class-feed.png) shows no halo or fringe of the original wall." Add a new K2_Q2 check: "No part of the instructor's hair, shoulders or arms is cut away along the cut-out edge on “Class announcement” (class-feed.png)." Keep H014 and H015 as the trap-specific checks.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Two facts in one check: the mark is the supplied drawing and not retyped, and it is scaled proportionally, not stretched or squashed. A stretched copy of the real drawing passes "not retyped" but fails "proportions unchanged".
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Modify each check: "The studio wordmark on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) is the verda_wordmark_transparent.png drawing, not retyped in another font." Add a new K2_Q2 check on each output: "The studio wordmark on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) is not stretched or squashed; its width-to-height ratio matches verda_wordmark_transparent.png." Do the same for class-feed.png and booking-story.png.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Exact pixel limits on a PNG (wordmark at most 34 px; safe area 250/320/60 px) cannot be judged by eye, and the validator flags them. They are fixed brief rules, so they cannot be retired. The wording has to tell the annotator to measure.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Keep the rules and make them measurable. H031: "Measured in an image editor, the studio wordmark's visible letterforms on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) are no more than 34 px tall." Use the same wording for class-feed H032 and booking-story H029. booking-story H001: "Measured in an image editor, every part of the booking action on “Studio booking story” (booking-story.png) is at least 250 px below the top edge, 320 px above the bottom edge and 60 px from each side."

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: "Only small labels may be Sage" is vague and states no standard. The brand rule names its standard: the field labels on passcard_2025_print.pdf.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Rewrite, for example studio-launch H037: "All type and the wordmark on Warm Off White #F4F0E8 on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) are Soft Ink #33352E; only short labels like the field labels on passcard_2025_print.pdf may be Sage." Add passcard_2025_print.pdf to reference_assets. Do the same on the other two outputs.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Wrong k_id. "The headline is the largest text" tests information hierarchy (K5_Q2), not primary-message recovery (K5_Q1).
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Set k_id to K5_Q2 on all three checks. Keep the text as is.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Wrong k_id. The upholstery-sage, floor-oak and one-daylight checks come from brand_identity.palette_rules.photography, and the coverage table lists them as brand rules B10 to B12. They are tagged K2_Q4 (identity fidelity), but the guide says brand rules are K2_Q3.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Set k_id to K2_Q3 on these nine checks. Keep the text as is.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Near-duplicate on the same output. H005 already requires every ground to be Warm Off White or Sage, and H063 restates that ground-colour fact. The only new fact in H063 is that none of the portrait's original wall shows.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Modify H063 so it holds only the new fact: "No part of the source portrait's original wall shows behind the cut-out instructor on “Class announcement” (class-feed.png); the ground is flat and solid." H005 keeps the colour rule.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Hard to read: each check spells out all six portrait filenames inline (33 to 36 words). The list hides the one fact being tested.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Shorten the list to a range, for example studio-launch H023: "If a supplied instructor portrait (verda_instructor_01.jpg to verda_instructor_06.jpg) appears on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png), the face keeps that portrait's features, with nothing reshaped or regenerated." Do the same for booking-story H022 and class-feed H006 and H009.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: "Clearer" is vague. It adds a second, loosely defined quality on top of the brightness fact, which is the one people can see.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Rewrite as one fact, for example: "Wherever verda_studio_frame_01.jpg or verda_studio_frame_02.jpg appears on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png), the room is visibly brighter than the dusky source frame, not left dark."

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: Part of a brand photography rule is untested. palette_rules.photography says "Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette", and the upholstery and floor are "neither pushed to the Sage or Oak hexes". Coverage rows B10 and B11 only paraphrase this as "its own sage green" and "its own natural oak". The checks they cite (H020, H024, H019 and the new floor-oak checks) only ask whether the upholstery reads sage green rather than blue or grey, and whether the floor reads oak rather than orange. A room frame washed flat to #9CA98F or #C7A97A, or an overall palette tint on a photo, passes every current check on all three outputs. The rule list has no row for it, so the coverage table hides the gap.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Add a rule row B20: "Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette; upholstery and floor are not pushed to the Sage or Oak hexes" (source: brand_identity.palette_rules.photography). Add one human K2_Q4 check per output and cite it in each cell, e.g. key l-no-palette-wash: "Wherever verda_studio_frame_01.jpg or verda_studio_frame_02.jpg appears on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png), the photo is not tinted toward the palette; upholstery and floor keep their own colour, not flat Sage #9CA98F or Oak #C7A97A." Add the same check as f-no-palette-wash for class-feed.png and s-no-palette-wash for booking-story.png. Use the same reference_assets as the floor-oak checks.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: Taking "from verda_wordmark_transparent.png" out of the fringe checks was right. As now worded, though, "clean letter edges, with no grey fringe" can fail the correct asset. palette_rules.opacity says "Supplied raster identity artwork retains its edge anti-aliasing", and that colour rules apply only to intentional recolouring. Annotators may read normal anti-aliased edge pixels as a grey fringe, or as off-palette colour under H033/H030. That would penalise a correct placement and blur what the verda_logo_web.png JPEG-ring trap is testing.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Reword H029 (launch), H030 (feed) and H027 (story) to: "The studio wordmark on “…” (….png) has clean letter edges, with no grey fringe or blocky compression ring; normal edge anti-aliasing is fine." Optionally add "intended" to H033/H030: "The intended type, wordmark, panel... colours come only from...".

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: Coverage row T08 marks the signature move na on class-feed and booking-story, with the reason "The brief asks for the separate above-headline lockup only on the launch page." But brand_identity.type_system.signature_move is not limited to one output: "Place [the wordmark] above the headline, on one line ..., no more than 34 px tall". The type scale also gives class-feed.png and booking-story.png a headline (H2). The coverage applies the "one line" and "34 px" parts of the same move to all three outputs (T09, T10) but drops "above the headline" for two of them, without saying why. The brief's "on the launch page ... as a separate lockup" can fairly be read as narrowing only the separate-lockup part.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Split T08. Keep "separate lockup" launch-only (H032). Add a rule row "The wordmark sits above the headline (signature move)" with K2_Q3 checks key f-mark-above-headline: "The studio wordmark on “Class announcement” (class-feed.png) sits above the headline." and s-mark-above-headline for booking-story.png. If the author decides the brief deliberately limits this to the launch page, rewrite both na reasons to quote that brief sentence and say the brief overrides the brand-wide signature move.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: Row R20 (cutout edge traps for verda_instructor_02.jpg and verda_instructor_05.jpg) is marked na on studio-launch and booking-story because "the brief commissions an instructor cutout only for the class announcement". Yet palette_rules.distribution expects that "a cut-out portrait sits on one of the two" grounds on any piece. Launch and story also already carry conditional portrait checks (studio-launch/H023, H025; booking-story/H022, H024). If either piece uses a cut-out of Dana Osei or Yuki Sato, the planned shoulder-bite and hair-fringe traps go unchecked there.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Add a conditional K2_Q2 check per output and cite it in the R20 cells in place of na. Key l-cutout-edge: "If an instructor cut-out appears on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png), its edge follows hair, shoulders and arms cleanly, with no bite into the figure and no halo." Add the same as s-cutout-edge for booking-story.png.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: Gap left by the roster trap. The asset_plan defect is "seven rows for six passes": Erin Coyle's row is a second RF-FND $34 entry. H006 lists the six classes and prices but does not forbid a repeated entry. A launch offer that shows Foundations $34 twice (from Erin's row, without her name) passes H006, H008 and H011.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Modify studio-launch/H006 to: "The class offer on “Studio launch-page composition” (studio-launch.png) lists exactly six classes, each once: Foundations $34, Flow $36, Core & Restore $34, Strength $38, Prenatal $36, Slow & Deep $34."

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: Retiring H005 (class offer above booking action) is correct: the brief makes the page hierarchy and booking-action placement designer choices. But its covered_by [studio-launch/H003, new:l-booking-visible] do not test the same fact. One tests that the action stays inside the edges, the other that it is present, not their order. The coverage chain therefore claims a cover that does not exist.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Keep the retirement. Change the why to say the requirement is dropped as not stated in the brief, and make clear that covered_by points to the remaining booking-action checks, not to an equivalent of the ordering rule. Leave covered_by empty if the validator allows it.
